security_spec.violation_condition: When QEMU TCG dispatches a synchronous exception (e.g. ECALL, page fault, misaligned access, illegal instruction) and the xivt.EHV bit is set but QEMU's trap dispatch does NOT check xivt.EHV before computing the exception entry point — either because (a) the EHV bit field in mivt/sivt is unimplemented and always reads 0, (b) QEMU reads the wrong privilege-level CSR (e.g., always checking mivt even in S-mode), or (c) the trap target address is computed as standard xtvec.BASE instead of xtvec.BASE + cause * 32
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: trap dispatch / exception entry point computation that references mtvec/stvec BASE without first reading (mivt|sivt) CSR bit 1 (EHV) to select between standard and hardware-vectored entry point calculation
security_spec.summary: Adding EHV bit to xivt CSRs (mivt/sivt) controls whether synchronous exceptions use hardware vectoring via xtvec offset; QEMU TCG must check this WARL bit at bit position 1 per-privilege-level when computing the trap entry point, or guest OS fast-exception-handling semantics break silently
